dataset: Government rules that make a programme harder or riskier for international students
notes: verified: 'official' = read on a government or university page; 'secondary' = news or a university adviser's summary only.
nationalities: ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes the rule applies to; 'nonLocal' = everyone without the host country's (or EU/EEA's) citizenship; null = everyone.
level: 'block' = the programme as designed may not be possible; 'high' = a real chance of refusal, delay or a lost benefit; 'notice' = a cost or condition to plan for.

rules.rule: Absence from Ireland should not exceed 90 days in a rolling year; students register only for the time they actually reside in Ireland and must be in Ireland to renew.
rules.effect: A compulsory term or semester abroad of 12-16 weeks (CEMS, exchange, double degree) breaks the 90-day limit for non-EEA students on Stamp 2; visa-required nationals may also need a new entry visa to return. UCD's MSc International Management (CEMS) director has said UCD can hardly admit students without EU/UK passports to CEMS for this reason.
rules.caveat: The official wording is 90 days in a rolling year. A dated September 2025 change and the '12 weeks over two years' framing come from UCD's programme director and were not found on an official page.

rules.rule: Students must show EUR 10,000 per year in available funds.
rules.effect: Proof of funds needed for the visa or registration.

rules.rule: Students on taught master's courses cannot bring dependants (spouse, children).
rules.effect: Applicants with a family who want them in the UK cannot do so on a taught master's.

rules.rule: The Graduate Route (post-study work visa) falls from 24 to 18 months for applications from 1 January 2027 (PhD graduates keep 3 years).
rules.effect: A master's starting in 2026 or later finishes after the change: 18 months of post-study work instead of 2 years.

rules.rule: Maintenance funds raised to GBP 1,529 a month in London and GBP 1,171 elsewhere.
rules.effect: More money to show for the visa.

rules.rule: An ATAS certificate is required for taught master's in listed sensitive subjects (by CAH3 code); EU/EEA, Swiss, Australian, Canadian, Japanese, New Zealand, Singaporean, South Korean and US nationals are exempt.
rules.effect: Extra clearance (weeks of processing; can be refused) for, among others, Chinese, Malaysian, Indian, Vietnamese, Indonesian and Myanmar nationals.
rules.nationalities: all except EU/EEA, CH, AU, CA, JP, NZ, SG, KR, US
rules.caveat: The library has no CAH3 codes yet; programmes are flagged by subject (computing, data/AI, engineering, construction) as 'check'.

rules.rule: Presidential proclamation suspending entry for nationals of listed countries (June 2025, expanded January 2026 to 39 countries); full ban includes Myanmar and Laos; partial-ban countries have F/M/J entry suspended.
rules.effect: Students from listed countries may be unable to get a student visa.
rules.caveat: Only the full-ban nationalities relevant to this tool's users are listed; check the current list for others.

rules.rule: Student visa interviews paused (29 May to 20 June 2025) and resumed with public social-media vetting.
rules.effect: Longer processing and a higher refusal risk for all F/J applicants.

rules.rule: The Secretary of State announced the US would aggressively revoke visas of Chinese students with Communist Party links or in critical fields.
rules.effect: Uncertainty for Chinese nationals in STEM programmes; no formal rule found.

rules.rule: National Planning Level of 295,000 for 2026 with Ministerial Direction 115: visa processing is slower for providers above their allocation.
rules.effect: Possible visa delays, depending on the university's allocation.

rules.rule: ETH Zurich and EPFL tripled tuition for foreign students from autumn 2025 (EPFL CHF 2,190 per semester).
2026 study-permit cap; master's and PhD students at public institutions no longer need a provincial attestation letter from 1 January 2026.
rules.effect: Low risk at public universities; college or private master's remain capped.
